text: We evaluated repeated self-distillation of the student's own labels, run for 2 distill rounds, with gpt2-medium as the weak supervisor and llama-3.1-8b as the strong student. Across 4 seeds, the method reached a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.82 with a standard error of 0.09, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.05; the margin over the baseline exceeds two standard errors of the measured PGR, so the effect is larger than the run-to-run spread we observed. Transfer accuracy was 0.87 (standard error 0.02), sitting between the weak supervisor's accuracy of 0.65 and the strong model's ceiling of 0.92. The main caveat is the small sample: with only 4 seeds, the standard errors are themselves imprecisely estimated, and no baseline standard error is reported, so the comparison rests on the point estimate for the baseline. Results are also specific to this single weak–strong model pairing and to 2 rounds of distillation.
